title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-03-02
source: Ampex MM-1000 16 Track Master Two Inch Wide Tape-Multi Track Mix-down  By Dan Healy @ 44.1KHz); DAT x ONE by Dick Latvala- DAT x TWO; Editing (Adobe Audition CC)-FLAC encoding(dBpoweramp)-Tagging(Tag & Re-name)by Jim Wise; This is a 100% Flat transfer from the DAT no signal processing what-so-ever

ai_review.summary: Near‑perfect soundboard capture of a high‑energy Fillmore West show featuring a primal jam and smoking Dark Star, with crystal‑clear instrument separation.
ai_review.review: The 16‑track soundboard mix delivers exceptional clarity – the guitars, Tom Constanten’s keyboards and the drums are wonderfully defined, making the Primal jam and Dark Star feel alive. Musically the show is a high‑energy snapshot of the Dead’s 1969 Fillmore run with standout moments like The Eleven, Feedback and That’s It for the Other One, though some reviewers note a few looser spots in Doin’ That Rag and the Alligator suite. Overall the performance is praised as one of the era’s best despite minor pitch‑speed quirks noted in alternate mixes.

ai_rating.rationale: Six out of seven reviews award 5 stars and highlight superb soundboard quality and strong performances; the lone 3‑star review notes only minor technical quirks, yielding an overall average above 4.5.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clean transfer with excellent instrument separation; reviewers call it near‑perfect and better than many other shows. Some alternate mixes exhibit pitch/speed wavers, but this 16‑track SBD is considered the cleanest version.

standout_songs: That's It for the Other One
show_quality.setlist_flow: Opens with an exploratory Dark Star, moves through classic mid‑tempo numbers and deep jams; the second set builds into extended improvisations before winding down with familiar closers. The flow is praised for its adventurous sequencing despite being a slightly weaker night compared to adjacent shows.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s tone and interplay with keyboards are highlighted as superb, especially on Dark Star and the Primal jam.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s keyboard work is noted for adding fresh sounds and being well‑balanced in the mix.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming is praised for its tightness and for providing a strong foundation to the post‑drum jam sections.
